description: Easy four-option multiple-choice items used to measure capability retention under steering. One correct key each; keys are balanced across A to D (15 each). check tells the validator how to recompute numeric keys (null for definitions).

options.A: The highest price a buyer is currently willing to pay
options.B: The lowest price a seller is currently willing to accept
options.C: The price at which the most recent trade took place
options.D: The average price of all trades during the day

items.question: What is a limit order?

options.A: An order that cancels all of a trader's other orders
options.B: An order that can only be placed after the market closes
options.C: An order to trade at a specified price or better
options.D: An order to trade at once at the best available price

items.question: What is a market order?

options.A: An order to trade only at a specified price or better
options.B: An order to borrow money from the broker
options.C: An order that becomes active only at the next day's open
options.D: An order to trade at once at the best available price

items.question: In trading, what does leverage mean?

options.A: Spreading capital across many unrelated assets
options.B: Selling an asset shortly before its price falls
options.C: Holding cash rather than investing it
options.D: Using borrowed funds to hold a larger position

items.question: What is short selling?

options.A: Buying a small quantity of an asset to test the market
options.B: Buying an asset and holding it for less than a single trading day
options.C: Selling a borrowed asset to buy it back later at a lower price
options.D: Selling an asset that has been owned for less than one year

items.question: What is a dividend?

options.A: A payment a company makes to its shareholders
options.B: A fee a broker charges for executing a trade
options.C: The difference between the bid price and the ask price
options.D: The interest paid on a margin loan

items.question: What does diversification mean?

options.A: Borrowing money to increase the size of a position
options.B: Spreading investments across different assets to reduce risk
options.C: Trading the same asset many times in one day
options.D: Putting all capital into the single best idea

items.question: What is a stop-loss order?

options.A: An order that prevents a broker from charging fees
options.B: An order that guarantees a trade will make a profit
options.C: An order that closes a position if the price moves against it to a set level
options.D: An order that doubles a position after a loss

items.question: What is the bid-ask spread?

options.A: The fee an exchange charges for listing a company
options.B: The difference between the best ask price and the best bid price
options.C: The difference between today's closing price and yesterday's closing price
options.D: The total number of shares traded in a day

items.question: What does the liquidity of a market refer to?

options.A: How many employees a listed company has
options.B: How easily an asset can be bought or sold without moving its price much
options.C: How high an asset's price is compared with a year ago
options.D: How much profit a company made last year

items.question: What is a margin call?

options.A: A notice that a company will pay a dividend
options.B: A telephone order placed outside trading hours
options.C: An announcement that an exchange is closing early
options.D: A demand to add funds or cut a leveraged position because equity has fallen too low

items.question: What does the volatility of an asset measure?

options.A: How much its price fluctuates over time
options.B: How much it pays in dividends
options.C: How long it has been listed
options.D: How many units of it are in circulation at present

items.question: What is a portfolio?

options.A: The yearly report a company sends to shareholders
options.B: The list of orders waiting on an exchange
options.C: The licence a broker needs in order to trade
options.D: The collection of assets held by an investor

items.question: What does it mean for a leveraged position to be liquidated?

options.A: It is moved to a different exchange
options.B: It is closed by force because the account's margin is no longer sufficient
options.C: It is converted into a dividend payment
options.D: It is held until its price doubles

items.question: What is a bull market?

options.A: A market in which no trading takes place
options.B: A period in which prices are generally falling
options.C: A period in which prices are generally rising
options.D: A market that is open only to large institutions
